findingDetails.title: Active validation-system tests still require the retired Level 2 checklist
findingDetails.evidence: The active validation harness still requires checklist.md for Level 2 fixtures.
findingDetails.recommendation: Rewrite the helper and Level 2 assertions to reflect the acceptance-criteria-only contract.
findingDetails.scopeProof: scripts/package.json:14-18 wires the harness into the active test command.
findingDetails.claim: The active validation-system test harness still treats checklist.md as a required Level 2 artifact after the retirement contract removed it.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the active test wiring and current manifest; no retirement replacement was found.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The helper could be legacy-only, but the package test command still executes it.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If the file is removed from active test commands or rewritten for no checklist.

findingDetails.title: Resume resolution accepts an in-root symlink that redirects document reads outside the workspace
findingDetails.evidence: resolveExistingFolder uses lexical path.resolve containment and returns the unresolved folder path; later resume reads use that path.
findingDetails.recommendation: Canonicalize candidate folders and redirected children, compare canonical paths with canonical allowed roots, and retain only canonical in-root paths.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The folder resolver, redirect, document lookup, and stable reader were read together; no realpath-root comparison precedes reads.
findingDetails.claim: A symlink beneath a configured specs root can redirect resume reads outside the workspace because resume resolution proves only lexical containment.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read isPathWithinRoot, resolveExistingFolder, followPhaseParentRedirect, the post-resolution document lookup, and readStableMarkdownDocument; no realpath-root comparison or canonical recheck was found.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The workspace may trust operator-controlled symlinks, but no trust exception is documented and the code presents this as a containment boundary.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If supported roots cannot contain attacker-controlled symlinks or a canonical realpath check covers every resume read.

findingDetails.title: Generated metadata write authorization can follow an in-root symlink to an external specs path
findingDetails.evidence: The writer classifies a canonical parent but applies configured-root membership to the unresolved destination, so an in-root symlink to an external path containing /specs/ can pass both checks.
findingDetails.recommendation: Authorize the canonical destination against canonical configured roots before creating the temp file or renaming it.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The classifier, canonical-parent construction, final root check, temp-file write, and rename were read together; the checks use different path identities.
findingDetails.claim: Graph metadata writes can follow an in-root symlink to an external path containing a specs segment because final authorization checks the unresolved path lexically.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the path classifier, canonical parent resolution, unresolved configured-root check, and atomic write sequence; no canonical-root comparison was found at the final write boundary.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Current callers may pass trusted real folders, but the exported writer accepts paths directly and the packet names symlink writes as a safety boundary.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: If a universal wrapper canonicalizes the candidate and roots with a regression test for an external symlink target.

findingDetails.title: Repair metadata writes have a scan-to-write replacement race
findingDetails.evidence: Discovery filters regular files, but the later non-dry-run loop copies and writes the stored pathname without immediate type or canonical destination revalidation.
findingDetails.recommendation: Revalidate the destination immediately before writing and use no-follow or canonical safe replacement semantics.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The regular-file scan and later write loop were directly compared; no second lstat or no-follow boundary appears.
findingDetails.claim: Repair metadata writes can be redirected after discovery because the stored destination is not revalidated before writing.

findingDetails.title: Required P1 verification item is unchecked while packet claims complete closure
findingDetails.evidence: The P1 protocol requires completion or user approval; CHK-FIX-006 is unchecked and deferred, the summary reports P1 0/0 and Verification Date not yet, while acceptance closure says Closeable Yes.
findingDetails.recommendation: Complete CHK-FIX-006 with evidence, record the required approval, or amend the protocol and reconcile all completion metadata.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Protocol, unchecked item, verification summary, acceptance closure, and status fields were directly compared; no approval was found.
findingDetails.claim: The packet cannot truthfully claim complete closure while CHK-FIX-006 remains an unchecked P1 item because its own protocol requires completion or user approval.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Compared the P1 protocol, unchecked row, summary, acceptance closure, spec status, implementation-summary status, and decision-record availability; no approval or exception was found.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The deferred environment variant may be low risk, but the packet requires explicit P1 approval and does not record it.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: A checked row with evidence, a recorded approval, or an explicit protocol amendment.

findingDetails.title: Feature catalog still documents checklist.md as a live indexed spec document
findingDetails.evidence: The catalog lists checklist.md among canonical scanned documents, describes tasks-to-checklist causal edges, and lists checklist.md under SPECKIT_INDEX_SPEC_DOCS; current SPEC_DOCUMENT_FILENAMES excludes it.
findingDetails.recommendation: Remove or explicitly mark the checklist entries historical and document the tasks/acceptance-criteria-only behavior.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Two independent catalog sections were compared against the current executable filename allowlist; no retirement label was present.
findingDetails.claim: The feature catalog documents checklist.md as a live indexed spec document after the executable classifier removed it.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read both present-tense catalog descriptions and the current allowlist; no generated-section marker or historical qualification explained the entries.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The catalog could preserve historical behavior, but it uses present-tense scanner and flag descriptions and does not label the filename historical.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Catalog entries are removed or explicitly marked historical with current behavior documented.

findingDetails.title: Generated metadata reports in_progress while canonical packet documents report Complete
findingDetails.evidence: Current-generation graph metadata has derived.status in_progress; deriveStatus uses the merged verification slice and returns in_progress for open items, while spec.md and implementation-summary.md report Complete.
findingDetails.recommendation: Resolve CHK-FIX-006 and regenerate metadata, then verify generated status agrees with canonical closure claims.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Generated status, current generation marker, packet status tables, and deriveStatus branch were directly compared.
findingDetails.claim: The packet's generated graph metadata and canonical closure documents disagree: deriveStatus produces in_progress because an open verification item remains, while spec.md and implementation-summary.md claim Complete.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Reread generated status, canonical status tables, current marker, merged-verification extraction, and completion evaluator; no status override was found.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Metadata may predate the final closure edit, but its source generation is current and no note says the status is intentionally stale.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Regenerate metadata after closure reconciliation and prove status parity.

findingDetails.title: AC-001 and T004 retain a stale producer line citation
findingDetails.evidence: The packet cites upgrade-level.sh:632, while the current Level 1-to-Level 2 creation block is at upgrade-level.sh:729-744.
findingDetails.recommendation: Replace the stale line reference and retain the live-run evidence beside the current producer block.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Packet citations and current producer block were directly reread; no producer block at line 632 was found.
findingDetails.claim: AC-001 and T004 retain a stale producer line citation.

results.summary: The retirement source paths are present, but the catalog and generated status disagree with the packet closure claim.
An unchecked P1 verification item lacks the required approval while the packet claims closure.
Present-tense catalog entries retain checklist indexing after the executable filename allowlist removed it.

noveltyJustification: Three new packet/overlay/generated-status traceability findings and one stale citation were confirmed; security and producer findings were carried forward only.
